prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2024 (policy-focused, non-ideological)

Immediate steps
- Fiscal stability with firm rules; OBR oversight at every fiscal event.
- 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week via evening/weekend sessions.
- New Border Security Command to target people-smuggling gangs.
- Great British Energy (publicly owned) to co-invest in clean power.
- Crackdown on antisocial behaviour and expansion of neighbourhood policing.
- Recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects.

Five missions
- Sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime; expand opportunity through education/childcare; build an NHS fit for the future.

Economic policy and business
- Industrial strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to leverage private investment in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, hydrogen.
- Business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; retain full expensing and AIA; replace business rates in England.
- Ten-year infrastructure strategy; new National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority.
- Planning reform to speed nationally significant infrastructure; gigabit and 5G nationwide by 2030.
- Rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; stronger bus franchising and option for municipal ownership; EV charging rollout and restore 2030 ICE phase-out date.
- AI regulation for frontier models; Regulatory Innovation Office; support for spinouts and R&D with 10-year budgets.
- Small business: tackle late payments; reform British Business Bank; easier access to procurement; Post Office strengthening and Horizon compensation.

Housing and local growth
- Build 1.5 million homes over the Parliament; restore mandatory targets; fund more planners via higher non-UK buyer surcharge.
- Brownfield first; strategic “grey belt” release with “golden rules”; new towns; stronger cross-boundary planning.
- Boost social/affordable housing; review Right to Buy discounts; protect new social homes.
- First-time buyer priority; permanent mortgage guarantee scheme.
- Private renting: end Section 21; empower renters to challenge unreasonable rent rises; raise standards. Leasehold reform: end new leasehold flats; move to commonhold; curb unfair charges.

Work, immigration, and skills
- Reduce net migration; reform points-based system; link shortage recruitment to domestic skills plans; stronger MAC.
- Employment support reform; youth guarantee (18–21) of training/apprenticeship/work support.
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours; end fire and rehire; day-one rights; Single Enforcement Body; minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living and remove adult age bands.
- Skills England; devolve adult skills; transform FE into Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with a flexible Growth and Skills Levy.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, long-duration storage, marine energy; maintain gas reserve; extend existing nuclear and proceed with Sizewell C and SMRs.
- No new oil and gas exploration licences; tighten and extend windfall tax; no fracking or new coal.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) and Local Power Plan for distributed generation.
- Grid upgrade and market reform; reduce standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; higher PRS efficiency standards by 2030.
- Nature: expand habitats; three new National Forests; nine National River Walks; circular economy.
- Water: tougher regulation, automatic fines, bonus blocks for polluters, independent monitoring.
- Farming: 50% of public food spend local or certified; workable ELM schemes; science-based bovine TB plan.
- Animal welfare: ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling/farming, snares; reduce animal testing.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders; stronger shoplifting and assault-on-retail-worker offences.
- Knife crime: mandatory YOT referral; bans on specific blades; enforce online sales rules; Young Futures hubs; youth workers in A&E/PRUs; new offence of child criminal exploitation.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist police units; fast-track rape courts; domestic abuse experts in 999; stalking protections; spiking offence.
- Police standards: mandatory vetting/misconduct rules; HMICFRS powers; fraud strategy; shared services/IT.
- Courts and prisons: expand prosecutors; sentencing review; build prison places; reduce reoffending via work, housing, and coordinated probation; strategic probation review.
- Address historical injustices (Hillsborough Law, Windrush, infected blood, Grenfell, Orgreave process).

NHS and social care
- Restore performance standards; independent sector capacity to cut waits; publish regular workforce plans.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; enhance clinical trials.
- Expand NHS app functionality; maternity safety focus; regulate NHS managers; implement Cass Review recommendations.
- Primary/community care shift: more GPs; continuity incentives; modern booking; pharmacy prescribing; direct referrals; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700k urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- National Care Service with national standards, “home first,” Fair Pay Agreement; family visit rights.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act; reduce suicide.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; restrict child-appeal vaping; curb junk-food ads to children; energy drink sales ban to under-16s; online safety enhancements; gambling regulation.
- Reduce health inequalities; women’s health priority; HIV action plan to end new cases by 2030.

Governance and devolution
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower ministerial standards adviser; modernise Commons; restrict MPs’ second jobs.
- Lords reform: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; stronger standards; consult on full replacement.
- Improve voter registration/ID consistency; votes at 16; donation rules strengthened.
- Reset intergovernmental relations; Council of the Nations and Regions; devolved funding frameworks; repeal/replace NI Legacy Act aligned with Stormont House.

Foreign, defence, and development
- NATO commitment; maintain nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review with path to 2.5% of GDP; defence industrial strategy; veterans support (including visa fee waivers after 4 years’ service).
- Support Ukraine (including frozen asset use); AUKUS; calibrated China strategy; protect Overseas Territories.
- EU: outside single market/customs union/FoM; improve trade (veterinary deal, MRAs, services), and security pact.
- Trade strategy; targeted FTAs and sector deals (e.g., India); WTO/CPTPP engagement; global minimum tax.
- Clean Power Alliance internationally; renew development leadership via FCDO; restore 0.7% GNI when fiscal conditions allow; focus on poverty, debt, women/girls, conflict prevention, climate finance.

Tax and enforcement
- No rises to NI, main Income Tax rates or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close carried interest and offshore IHT loopholes; modernise HMRC and tighten anti-avoidance; recover Covid fraud.
